items.summary: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, July 31, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer A projectile struck the engine room of the Liberia-flagged crude oil tanker Dominica Prosperity off the United Arab Emirates on Wednesday, forcing the evacuation of all 22 crew members as emergency crews battled a fire aboard the vessel. The attack was one of four tanker incidents documented in the latest maritime security advisory covering the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz, including a separate strike that left multiple seafarers injured. India’s Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, identified the vessel as the Dominica Prosperity and confirmed that 19 Indian nationals were among the 22 crew members rescued by the UAE Coast Guard. In its November 12 advisory update, the Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) documented four tanker attacks since its previous report, including two in the Persian Gulf and two in the Strait of Hormuz. One of the incidents involved the tanker Fujairah Energy , which was struck by an unknown projectile while traveling eastbound in the Arabian Gulf on November 10. JMIC said the latest attacks bring the number of recorded maritime security incidents since March 1 to 181, underscoring the continuing dangers facing commercial vessels operating in the region.

items.summary: French logistics group GEODIS has launched a new rail freight service between Vicenza, in northeastern Italy, and Noisy-le-Sec, in the Paris area. The train is operated by Captrain and Hexafret, both part of SNCF’s Rail Logistics Europe, and currently runs once a week in each direction, with a second weekly departure planned from January 2027. The first train left on 19 October, GEODIS said in a press release. According to GEODIS, the service cuts CO2 emissions per shipment by 80% on average compared to an all-road diesel solution. The new line brings to northeastern Italy a solution that GEODIS already offers to companies in Lombardy, Piedmont and Emilia-Romagna through its connection departing from Novara. That service was launched in January 2022 and also terminates in Noisy-le-Sec, east of Paris. “Rail is an efficient mode of transport, especially over long distances, with much lower CO2 emissions than road transport”, said Jean-François Ancora, Managing Director of Captrain Italia. Bilateral trade in goods and services between France and Italy reached €136 billion in 2025, with Italy being France’s fourth-largest trading partner and France Italy’s second, according to GEODIS. With one weekly departure, the new line remains a modest service for now, but the planned doubling in January 2027 suggests GEODIS expects demand from Veneto shippers to grow.

Revenue in its liner shipping segment rose 25% year on year in Q3, “driven by a significantly higher average freight rate of $1,808 per teu”, compared with $1,413 per teu in the same period last year. Its third-quarter volumes reached 3.4m, marginally below last year and clearly below the global market – Container Trades Statistics (CTS) recently released Q3 data showed global volumes growing 5% year on year . However, Hapag-Lloyd CEO Rolf Habben Jansen said the period had seen exceptionally high levels of vessel utilisation, which had supported the higher freight prices. The carrier appeared to struggle on some of its core lanes – Asia-Europe volumes declined 5.7%, compared with Q3 25, to 927,000 teu, while its transpacific volumes also contracted, by 2.7%, to 1.2m teu. Hapag-Lloyd also reported a 35.1% increase in the average freight rate for these trades.

items.title: Spanish box terminals face cargo backlog after general strike
items.original_title: Spanish box terminals face cargo backlog after general strike
items.summary: Spain’s container terminals are beginning the task of recovering following yesterday’s general strike across the country that left box ships waiting at anchor after a slew of terminal closures – but the extent of the cargo backlog remains unclear. Container movements ground to a halt at Algeciras, loading and discharge was suspended at Valencia, and cargo operations requiring the support of dockers stopped at Barcelona, although essential marine services remained unaffected. Trade union confederation CCOO’s maritime-sector representative in Valencia for vessel operations, Francisco Martínez, told reporters: “There are no workers available, and there are no vessel operations.” And while one forwarder told The Loadstar the strikes had “zero” impact on their operations, AIS tracking data showed the 1,072 teu Contship Zen still at anchor off Valencia last night, with an expectation of berthing this morning. The scale and duration of any backlog will depend on how quickly terminals restore normal productivity, and whether carriers have had to revise their rotations or roll cargo, but requests by The Loadstar to glean this information from terminal operators today have fallen on deaf ears. Operations at both APMT’s Algeciras and Total Terminal International Algeciras were halted between 2am on 11 November and 2am on 12 November, bringing container movements to a standstill at one of the major Mediterranean transhipment hubs.

items.title: Wave of larger newbuild box ships a threat to the panamax fleet
items.original_title: Wave of larger newbuild box ships a threat to the panamax fleet
items.summary: The coming influx of larger containerships could render ageing panamax vessels commercially obsolete by 2030, while carriers’ efforts to renew smaller fleets threaten further capacity displacement. Jonathan Roach, analyst at Braemar, told The Loadstar the newbuilding programme was creating a substantial mismatch between vessels entering service and those approaching retirement. He identified the 4,000–7,499 teu segment as particularly vulnerable, with 428 vessels aged at least 20 years old against just 283 ships on order. Mr Roach said: “The ageing fleet is concentrated in the sub-panamax segment, while the orderbook is heavily skewed towards larger ships.” He warned that traditional panamax and post-panamax vessels could become increasingly squeezed, “potentially becoming obsolete by 2030”. Mr Pape-Leostic said: “In our view, this renewal will not be on a like-for-like basis,” and explained that carriers historically deploying vessels below 1,000 teu, could replace them with ships of 1,200 teu or even 1,800 teu. The figures suggest that the replacment of older vessels with larger ships could increase the global fleet’s carrying capacity without an increase in vessel numbers. Alphaliner’s data also shows the largest newbuildings dominating capacity additions, with 291 ships of at least 18,000 teu on order, representing 6.06m teu.

Marine Platforms now expects to take complete ownership within the next two years as it looks to strengthen its subsea construction capabilities in West Africa and other international markets. (Source: Courtesy of Kjell-Bendik Pedersen) The European Union paid an estimated €8.7 billion for liquefied natural gas from Russia’s Yamal project in the first 10 months of 2026, exceeding the estimated total for all of 2025, as the countdown to a ban on Russian LNG imports enters its final weeks. EU ports received 12.89 million tonnes across 177 cargoes between January and October, up 6.3% from the same period last year, according to an analysis by environmental group Urgewald using Kpler shipping data. The estimated bill is around 21% higher than the €7.2 billion calculated for all of 2025 . But the more immediate challenge for Yamal LNG, operated by Russian producer Novatek, is logistical. The EU ban on Russian LNG imports under eligible existing long-term contracts takes effect on January 1, forcing the project to redirect cargoes toward Asia just as winter ice makes eastbound navigation along the Northern Sea Route increasingly difficult. Yamal depends on 14 specialized Arc7 ice-class LNG carriers, which can operate in Arctic waters and return quickly from nearby European terminals. The January ban will not necessarily stop Yamal LNG exports, but it will remove the project’s most convenient winter market.

items.title: Why shipowners might be better off sharing profits than taking on debt
items.original_title: Why shipowners might be better off sharing profits than taking on debt
items.summary: Traditional loans demand repayments regardless of freight markets. Earnings-sharing structures offer a different proposition: investors participate in a vessel’s fortunes while owners retain control. Captain Vikas Pandey from Shipfinex explains. Small and mid-sized owners, who by one industry estimate own up to 60% of the world’s ships, still meet low advance ratios on older tonnage, higher margins, or alternative lenders asking for equity kickers and profit participation on top of interest. Earnings-sharing tends to make sense where bank debt is unavailable or priced close to equity; where the vessel has visible employment, such as a period charter, that investors can underwrite; where the owner needs to protect liquidity through the cycle; or where equity is locked in an unencumbered vessel that the owner wants to release without selling. Before signing, owners should settle the definition of net earnings and deductible costs, the treatment of off-hire and drydocking, reserve funding, the term and any cap on investor returns, buy-back rights, and what happens on a sale or total loss. Where a first-priority registered ship mortgage is in place, the mortgagee’s consent is required and investor distributions rank behind debt service. Debt remains the cheapest capital in shipping for owners who can get it on good terms.

items.title: NYK charts the great reshuffling of global commodity trades
items.original_title: NYK charts the great reshuffling of global commodity trades
items.summary: One of the world’s largest shipowners has given its take on where it sees the gas, dry bulk, and tanker markets heading in the coming years. The global VLCC fleet will see a significant expansion despite the extraordinary earnings currently being enjoyed by tanker owners, with Japanese shipping giant Nippon Yusen Kaisha (NYK) forecasting the delivery of approximately 290 supertankers between 2026 and 2029. NYK’s research group unveiled its latest shipping market outlook yesterday, predicting that the active VLCC fleet will increase from 909 vessels at the end of 2025 to 1,082 by the end of 2029, a rise of 19%. The forecast assumes a substantial number of ageing vessels will leave the market, but deliveries are expected to be comparable to those witnessed during the shipping boom of the 2000s. NYK’s research also anticipates a fundamental restructuring of global commodity trades over the coming decade. Seaborne iron ore volumes are forecast to decline from 1.65bn tonnes in 2025 to 1.40bn tonnes in 2035 as Chinese steel production contracts. Coal shipments are forecast to fall from 1.33bn tonnes to 1.04bn tonnes over the same period, with thermal coal accounting for most of the decline. LNG is heading in the opposite direction, with seaborne volumes expected to climb from 433m tonnes to 622m tonnes by 2035.

items.summary: Bunker prices have plunged by as much as 20% in less than two weeks as hopes of an easing of the Iran conflict send oil markets tumbling, offering shipowners some relief from what is still expected to be the most expensive year for marine fuel on record. Singapore very low sulphur fuel oil (VLSFO) was assessed by Ship & Bunker at $814.50 a tonne yesterday, down from $1,019.50 on October 30, a drop of $205, or 20.1%. The retreat represents a saving of $615,000 on a 3,000-tonne bunker stem compared with the end of last month. Splash reported on November 3 that Singapore VLSFO had climbed back above $1,000 a tonne for the first time since March, with the Iran conflict having almost doubled bunker prices since February. Despite the latest retreat, Singapore fuel remains approximately 56% more expensive than immediately before the war began on February 28. Meanwhile, Clarksons Research has put shipping’s total bunker bill this year at a record $220bn. Speaking at the IBIA Annual Convention in New York yesterday, Clarksons Research managing director Steve Gordon estimated the global bunker market at 290m tonnes annually. Fuel demand is rising again despite modern ships being around 50% more efficient than vessels built 15 years ago.

items.title: Singapore Strait robbery spike sparks fresh security warning
items.original_title: Singapore Strait robbery spike sparks fresh security warning
items.summary: A sudden resurgence in robberies aboard merchant ships in the Singapore Strait has prompted regional maritime security authorities to issue an urgent warning, with three vessels boarded in nine days and one seafarer injured. The ReCAAP Information Sharing Centre issued an incident alert yesterday following attacks on two bulk carriers and a tanker between November 2 and 10, warning that further incidents are possible. All three robberies occurred in the eastbound lane of the Traffic Separation Scheme, within approximately 3.2 nautical miles of each other. The first incident involved the bulk carrier Star Calypso, boarded at 2125 hrs on November 2. The second, involving the bulk carrier APJ Priti 2, took place late on November 4, followed by an attack on the tanker Salsa in the early hours of November 10. The latest incidents bring the number of robberies reported in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore this year to 28. ReCAAP is urging Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore to intensify patrols and surveillance, improve coordination and share intelligence to identify and arrest those responsible. Shipmasters have been advised to maintain heightened vigilance, particularly during darkness, and strengthen preventive measures, including CCTV coverage of potential boarding locations. The organisation is also encouraging vessels to report suspicious activity immediately and use its digital reporting and incident mapping systems when assessing voyage risks.

It is also a technology milestone, with the MEGCs incorporating the first Type IV glass-fibre pressure cylinders manufactured in China. The shipment is an important step in UAC’s global growth strategy, moving its Jiaxing facility from production ramp-up into commercial delivery for international customers. UAC has more than two decades of experience in Type IV glass-fibre technology, with more than 12,000 cylinders in operation across more than 40 countries. “This shipment to Australia is an important milestone in UAC’s global strategy. The Hiringa shipment demonstrates that our dual-manufacturing strategy is now translating into commercial delivery for international customers,” said Lars Erik Lunøe, CEO of UMOE Advanced Composites. UAC previously supplied Type IV MEGCs manufactured in Norway for Hiringa Energy’s first four operating hydrogen refuelling stations in New Zealand.

items.title: Geneva Dry: Belships’ Ivar Hansson Myklebust on China’s changing commodities role
items.original_title: Geneva Dry: Belships’ Ivar Hansson Myklebust on China’s changing commodities role
items.summary: Ivar Hansson Myklebust, chair and CEO of Norway’s Belships, believes the shipping industry continues to underestimate the growth potential of developing economies. Ahead of his appearance at Geneva Dry 2027, he discusses China’s changing trading patterns, fleet supply and the opportunities emerging across minor bulks. A changing China, resilient emerging economies and a relatively predictable fleet supply picture will be among the biggest themes shaping dry bulk shipping when the industry gathers in Geneva next April, according to Ivar Hansson Myklebust. China’s changing role in dry bulk shipping is another development he believes deserves closer attention. On technology, Myklebust sees opportunities less in revolutionary developments than in improving everyday shipping processes, from maintenance planning to freight collection. Myklebust will join the Minor Bulks panel at Geneva Dry on Wednesday, April 28, alongside Emilie Nourry of Eramet, Malgorzata Gill of Holcim Trading, S.K. For Myklebust, the value of Geneva Dry lies in bringing together the different sides of the commodities shipping business. “And meeting market participants from all sides of the business is never a waste of time.” Geneva Dry 2027, the world’s premier commodities shipping conference, takes place at the Hotel President Wilson on April 27 and 28 with organisers today unveiling limited special discount rates at the five-star hotel for signed-up delegates.

items.title: Russian Diesel Faces U.S. Buyer Resistance Despite Trump Sanctions Waiver
items.original_title: Russian Diesel Faces U.S. Buyer Resistance Despite Trump Sanctions Waiver
items.summary: HOUSTON, Nov 11 (Reuters) – US companies are unlikely to import Russian diesel as a tanker full of the fuel idles off the US Eastern Seaboard, experts said, despite President Donald Trump’s temporary waiver of some sanctions on Moscow’s fuel exports. Banks are likely to be reluctant to finance US deals for Russian diesel, the experts said, noting there are legal questions about whether the president’s waiver is enough to allow for the imports. There are also operational challenges, because importers would need to blend the Russian diesel to meet US heating oil specifications. That is down 20 cents a gallon from $6.33 the day that Trump waived the sanctions in October but up 63% from $3.76 before the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February, according to AAA data. A Trump administration official said the temporary waiver was in compliance with all applicable laws. Banks are unlikely to finance deals related to a Russian diesel trade, which could violate sanctions in other countries, said David Tannenbaum, director of sanctions consultancy Blackstone Compliance Services and a former US Treasury sanctions specialist.

items.summary: Trafigura-backed tanker owner Volare Shipping has agreed to acquire a VLCC newbuilding from an affiliate of its controlling shareholder for $210m, adding another supertanker to its expanding fleet just weeks after its Oslo market debut. The Euronext Growth-listed company said it had struck a deal for the scrubber-fitted Veni Vidi Vici , which is currently undergoing sea trials at Hengli Heavy Industry in China. The seller is an affiliate of Trafigura Maritime Logistics, Volare’s indirect majority shareholder. The transaction is expected to close this month, subject to financing and customary conditions. The acquisition will take Volare’s operating fleet to seven modern VLCCs, with another eight newbuildings scheduled to join through 2028. The Singapore-incorporated company was launched by Trafigura in September and subsequently raised $500m in an Oslo private placement. It entered the market with six trading VLCCs and eight newbuildings, with Trafigura retaining majority control and commercial management. The latest purchase brings its projected fleet to 15 ships and extends an ordering and acquisition campaign that has made the commodity trader an increasingly prominent player in the crude tanker market.

items.title: IMO Chief Calls for Strict Enforcement of SOLAS Rules in Strait of Hormuz
items.original_title: IMO Chief Calls for Strict Enforcement of SOLAS Rules in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: FILE PHOTO: Oil/Chemical Tanker "Bald Man" at the Port of Fujairah, as the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran limits marine traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, May 6, 2026. REUTERS/Amr Alfiky/File Photo International Maritime Organization (IMO) Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez has called on governments to step up enforcement of international maritime regulations in the Strait of Hormuz, warning that unsafe shipping practices are adding to the risks facing seafarers amid the ongoing conflict. In a statement issued Wednesday, Dominguez raised concerns about vessels transiting the strategic waterway without complying with basic international safety requirements, including provisions of the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS). The warning comes as commercial shipping continues to face attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz, where the IMO has now verified more than 130 incidents involving merchant vessels since the conflict began on February 28. The IMO chief specifically cited reports of substandard vessels, ships concealing their IMO identification numbers, vessels operating under fraudulent registrations or false flags, and other unsafe practices. The latest appeal follows last week’s meeting of the IMO Council in London, where member states called for stronger protections for seafarers and reiterated that vital shipping lanes must remain open, safe and secure.

items.title: UK Launches ‘Atlantic Net’ to Track Russian Submarines and Protect Undersea Cables
items.original_title: UK Launches ‘Atlantic Net’ to Track Russian Submarines and Protect Undersea Cables
items.summary: The UK is moving ahead with a £90 million investment in autonomous underwater systems, advanced sensors and artificial intelligence to strengthen the Royal Navy’s ability to track Russian submarines and protect critical infrastructure in the North Atlantic. The initiative, known as Atlantic Net, is the first operational phase of the Royal Navy’s broader Atlantic Bastion programme, which aims to combine crewed warships and submarines with autonomous systems to improve underwater surveillance and counter potential threats to subsea communications cables, energy networks and shipping routes. The UK Ministry of Defence announced the investment Tuesday during the International Sea Power Conference in Oslo, Norway, alongside a framework agreement with UK-based marine robotics company Ocean Infinity Solutions. The system will combine underwater sensors, uncrewed platforms, communications technology and AI-powered data analysis to detect and track potentially hostile submarine activity. The programme is expected to become operational in 2027, according to UK Defence Minister Luke Pollard, who outlined the plans in a speech in Oslo. “This investment gives the Royal Navy new technology to find threats earlier and protect our critical infrastructure, while also backing British business.” The investment comes amid growing concern among European governments and NATO allies over the vulnerability of underwater infrastructure, particularly communications cables and energy connections that are essential to both civilian economies and military operations.

items.title: Ports could future-proof to beat box terminal congestion
items.original_title: Ports could future-proof to beat box terminal congestion
items.summary: In recent months, a daily review of container terminal utilisation levels has become something of a ‘must-read’ for supply chain planners seeking to understand where boxes may be delayed, and for how long. That remains an art rather than science, but indicates how the container shipping industry has experienced something of a paradigm shift into an era in which waves of mega-congestion ripple across the port and shipping system. Terminal occupancy levels – ie, how many containers are sitting in a yard awaiting either a truck or loading on a vessel – continue to sit way above what these facilities were designed to handle. Some of this is beyond terminal operators’ control – they have no say over when vessels arrive, or how delayed they might have been at the previous port; while wars, weather, and other disruptive events are in the hands of the gods – or people who think of themselves as such… However, in the spirit of supply chain resilience, they could be far better prepared to tackle congestion when it arises.

items.title: UK taps Ocean Infinity for subsea security push
items.original_title: UK taps Ocean Infinity for subsea security push
items.summary: UK-based marine robotics specialist Ocean Infinity has been selected as the Royal Navy’s commercial mission partner for a new underwater surveillance programme backed by an initial £90m ($120m) investment. The company will work with the Royal Navy to develop Atlantic Net, a network of autonomous maritime systems, underwater sensors and artificial intelligence designed to monitor the North Atlantic and protect critical subsea infrastructure. The programme forms the first operational phase of the Royal Navy’s wider Atlantic Bastion initiative, which aims to combine crewed warships with autonomous and remotely operated systems. The Ministry of Defence said the framework agreement with Ocean Infinity would pave the way for the £90m investment and support almost 200 skilled jobs. The system is expected to become operational in 2027, providing Royal Navy warships and Astute-class submarines with earlier warnings of potential underwater threats. Ocean Infinity will work with specialist partners to combine maritime platforms, underwater sensing, communications, remote operations, and data services into a persistent surveillance capability. The company operates a fleet of remotely operated and lean-crewed vessels used for offshore surveys and subsea operations. One of its Armada vessels participated in Royal Navy trials earlier this year. The initial programme will also draw on UK technology suppliers, with much of the equipment expected to come from small and medium-sized businesses.

items.title: Monjasa seals biggest-ever fleet deal with five-tanker swoop
items.original_title: Monjasa seals biggest-ever fleet deal with five-tanker swoop
items.summary: Danish bunker supplier and shipowner Monjasa has acquired five sister product tankers from Germany’s Bernhard Schulte in its largest-ever fleet deal, strengthening its marine fuels operations in West Africa. The Fredericia-based group has picked up five 2010- and 2011-built tankers of around 16,500 dwt each. The purchase price has not been disclosed. Four vessels, renamed Monjasa Tracer, Monjasa Tuner, Monjasa Twister and Monjasa Tracker , have already joined the fleet and are trading in West Africa and Northwest Europe. The fifth, Monjasa Trigger , is set to follow by the end of November. The acquisition takes Monjasa’s owned fleet to 20 tankers, alongside around 10 ships on time charter. Group chief executive Anders Østergaard described the purchase as the company’s largest single tonnage acquisition, highlighting the benefits of taking on five identical vessels with established operating costs and technical requirements. “Finding five sister vessels of this quality, at competitive market terms and with an operating profile that fits our existing fleet, is not something you come across every day,” he said. The deal builds on Monjasa’s earlier tanker investments in West Africa, including the 2023 acquisition of the 68,589 dwt Monjasa Leader and the 13,051 dwt Monjasa Refiner , which were brought in for floating storage and bunker supply operations, respectively.

items.title: Coal’s new world order takes shape
items.original_title: Coal’s new world order takes shape
items.summary: Coal’s changing trade map is creating winners and losers across dry bulk shipping in 2026, with Indonesian exports retreating, southern African shipments setting records and Asian import demand increasingly fractured. Clarksons Research forecasts seaborne coal trade will edge up just 1% this year to 1.343bn tonnes. Beneath that modest increase, Indonesian exports are projected to fall 6% to 496.9m tonnes, while Australian shipments climb 4% to 371.3m tonnes. BIMCO reports coal imports dropped 7% in the first ten months despite coal-fired electricity generation rising around 9%. BRS says coal inventories at power stations were equivalent to only 5.9 days of consumption, against 14.7 days a year earlier. Supramaxes have been hardest hit, with Indian-bound coal volumes falling 16%, compared with a 4% decline for panamaxes. October offered the first signs of a turn, with Indian seaborne coal arrivals rising 7% year-on-year. However, BIMCO expects only a limited import recovery in 2027 as domestic mining grows.

items.title: Hapag’s standalone Asia-Mexico string adds another spoke to Gemini hub network
items.original_title: Hapag’s standalone Asia-Mexico string adds another spoke to Gemini hub network
items.summary: Hapag-Lloyd has presented AMX, its new Asia–Mexico service, as standalone: its own ships; its own rotation of Ningbo-Qingdao-Busan-Ensenada-Manzanillo-Lázaro Cárdenas-Ningbo; launching in January 2027. Standalone is the word the press release leans on, and it is the one worth questioning. AMX is standalone the way a spoke is standalone – Hapag owns the vessels, but it can only fill an 8,000 teu ship on this run because the Gemini hub network it operates with Maersk gives the cargo somewhere to come from. The hub-and-spoke network it now runs with Maersk supplies the missing pieces – balancing cargo through the Gemini hubs and relay connections onward, so AMX does not have to source a full, self-sufficient ship at Asian load ports. The simple answer to ‘why standalone’ and ‘why 2027’ is that the network to support a self-controlled spoke only recently came together. Each is an owned loop made to clip onto the Gemini backbone, and the method is consistent — control the vessel, fill it through the hubs. That slice is not small: I estimate Hapag’s allocation on MSC’s loops is worth around 8,375 teu of nominal vessel capacity, call it some 7,000 teu of usable space for its customers once a ship is realistically loaded.

items.title: Panama Canal turns the taps back on
items.original_title: Panama Canal turns the taps back on
items.summary: The Panama Canal has raised its daily transit capacity to 34 vessels and increased the maximum allowable draft for neopanamax ships to 50 ft, marking another significant easing of restrictions following an exceptionally wet October. The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) confirmed that an additional booking slot for super-category vessels at the original panamax locks would increase their daily allocation from 18 to 19. Total availability now stands at 24 slots through the panamax locks and 10 through the larger neopanamax locks, up from a combined 33 previously. The maximum neopanamax draft has meanwhile increased from 49 ft to 50 ft (15.24 m), effective immediately and until further notice. Data compiled by Ursa Shipbrokers showed Gatun Lake averaged 85.80 ft (26.15 m) during October, just 0.15 ft below its historical average and more than 6 ft higher than during the drought-stricken October of 2023. Rainfall across the canal watershed during the first 29 days of October was 8.4% above the 30-year average and 83.6% greater than the corresponding period three years ago. The turnaround is particularly striking given the dire outlook during August, when weak rainfall and a strengthening El Niño forced authorities to slash daily booking capacity to 32 vessels and impose tighter draft restrictions.

items.title: Russian crude exports fall on G7 tankers as Greek operators flee for better earnings
items.original_title: Russian crude exports fall on G7 tankers as Greek operators flee for better earnings
items.summary: Russian crude exports on G7 tankers fell sharply in October as Greek operators were enticed by strong earnings elsewhere and steered away from Black Sea conflicts, according to S&P Global Commodities at Sea(opens in a new tab) and Maritime Intelligence Risk Suite data. The data shows tankers flagged, owned or operated by companies based in G7 countries and their allies, or insured by Western protection and indemnity clubs, loaded roughly 906,000 barrels per day of Russian crude in October, or 24.2% of total exports. The share was the lowest in seven months. In September, G7 tankers lifted 1.2 million b/d, or 29.2% of total exports. October’s average Suezmax time-charter-equivalent earnings for transporting Russian crude from the Baltic to West Coast India was $46,257.92 per day lower than the Global Suezmax Index, compared with a discount of $23,225.69/day in September, according to Platts assessments for non-scrubber, non-eco ships. Greek tanker firms have also been avoiding operations in the Black Sea, with the CAS/MIRS data showing only one Greek-operated tanker lifting Russian crude in the region last month, compared with 11 in other regions. Platts assessed the additional war risk premium for crude exports from the Black Sea at $5/b on Nov.

items.title: Korea shipbuilders face LNG carrier price squeeze as North America orders seen next year
items.original_title: Korea shipbuilders face LNG carrier price squeeze as North America orders seen next year
items.summary: LNG carriers are the flagship high-margin vessel type where Korean shipbuilders have shown strength. According to Clarksons Research, the ship new building price for a 174,000-cubic-meter LNG carrier fell from an average of $248 million in January this year to $245 million in October. In fact, contract prices for newbuild LNG carriers at Samsung Heavy Industries, which has the most LNG carrier orders among Korean shipbuilders, have dropped from late last year and early this year. At its third-quarter earnings briefing on the 29th of last month, Samsung Heavy Industries acknowledged it had recently taken LNG carrier orders at low prices. Some analysts say China’s rising share of LNG carrier orders is pressuring Korean shipbuilders to lower prices. On the decline in Korea’s market share and prices due to China’s rising LNG carrier orders, Samsung Heavy Industries said it is “carefully monitoring developments in China.” Bae Gi-yeon, an analyst at Meritz Securities, said, “Capacity expansion and new entrants at Chinese shipyards are putting downward pressure on the ship new building price for LNG carriers,” adding, “The pricing competitiveness of low-cost LNG carriers from Chinese shipyards is bound to stand out.” The broader base of Chinese yards is forcing Korean shipbuilders to cut prices to win orders.

items.title: Carriers may secure only part of their November rate increases as Suez returns, Sogese report says
items.original_title: Carriers may secure only part of their November rate increases as Suez returns, Sogese report says
items.summary: Freight rates to Europe have rebounded since early October after falling steadily from their July peak, but the conditions behind the rebound are mixed. Cargo demand is positive, with Far East to Europe volumes up 12.2% in the first seven months of the year, according to Xeneta. Ships, however, are arriving late, and the return of Suez routings is releasing capacity faster than schedules are recovering. In its November Europe Container Market Update, Sogese reads this as a market moving from a disruption premium to a capacity-management test, in which the price carriers announce and the price shippers actually pay are drifting apart. If Suez keeps normalising, the key question for 2027 will not be whether there are enough ships, but how aggressively carriers manage the capacity that comes back into the market.”Andrea Monti, CEO & MD, Sogese 2. For its November outlook the report also sets out three paths: partial uptake of announced increases, failure of the increases to reach market rates, and uneven capacity and pricing as Suez rotations are rebuilt. Treat Drewry’s 12 and 19 November releases and the expiry of the 1 to 14 November FAKs as the first evidence of what the market will pay.

items.title: Ports of LA/LB, watchmen extend contract through 20 November as negotiations continue
items.original_title: Ports of LA/LB, watchmen extend contract through 20 November as negotiations continue
items.summary: Negotiations continue amid an effort to avoid a work stoppage at the West Coast ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach (LA/LB), and the union and the ports have agreed to extend their contract through 20 November. International Longshore and Warehouse Union (ILWU) Local 26, the union representing about 250 port watchmen at the ports of LA/LB, and the Pacific Maritime Association (PMA), which represents employers, will continue negotiating a new contract during the extension. Should the watchmen strike, operations at eight terminals in the port complex could be brought to a halt. Watchmen make up only 2% of ILWU workers at the two ports but work at terminals handling roughly 85% of Long Beach’s cargo and 33% of Los Angeles’ cargo. It is the third extension after the watchmen originally planned to strike on 4 November. Negotiations will continue with the assistance of the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service (FMCS), PMA said in a statement on its website. The watchmen are not part of the agreement reached in 2023 between 29 West Coast ports and 22,000 workers that expires in 2028. Titanium dioxide (TiO2) is also shipped in containers. Source: ICIS by Adam Yanelli, https://www.icis.com/explore/resources/news/2026/11/09/11241010/ports-of-la-lb-watchmen-extend-contract-through-20-november-as-negotiations-continue/

items.title: China’s October Crude Oil Imports Rise to Highest Level Since March Amid Middle East War
items.original_title: China’s October Crude Oil Imports Rise to Highest Level Since March Amid Middle East War
items.summary: China’s October oil imports fell 13.3% from a year earlier but reached the highest level since March this year after the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted supplies from the Middle East, official data showed on Tuesday. China, the world’s biggest oil buyer, imported 41.94 million metric tons of crude oil in October, or 9.88 million barrels per day, ⁠with the daily ⁠import rate up 9.4% from September, according to data from the General Administration of Customs. China’s oil product exports, including gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and fuel oil, fell to 5.18 million ⁠tons in October from 7.16 million tons in September, but were up 14.6% from a year earlier, according to the data. Refined oil product exports in the first 10 months of the year totaled 46.59 million tons, down 2% from a year earlier. Oil product imports rose to 3.15 million tons in October from ⁠1.85 ⁠million tons in September. January-to-October imports fell to 27.15 million tons from 34.19 million tons a year earlier. Data also showed that natural gas imports, including liquefied natural gas and pipeline gas, rose 2.4% from a year earlier to 10.01 million tons in October. January-to-October natural gas imports totaled 99.22 million metric tons, down 2.8% from a year earlier. Source: Asharq Al-Awsat

items.title: COP31: Broad maritime coalition launches breakthrough 20% electrification goal by 2035
items.original_title: COP31: Broad maritime coalition launches breakthrough 20% electrification goal by 2035
items.summary: COP31 presents an electrification goal: raising the share of global final energy demand met by electricity to 35% by 2035 (up from just over 20%), cutting fossil fuel dependence, and driving sector transitions. Many international and regional initiatives, coalitions and alliances already promote maritime decarbonization. This Maritime Electrification Breakthrough Goal aims to align political and collective action to accelerate the deployment and expansion of electrification. Our Shared Goal We, representing the maritime sector from across the value chain, support the COP31 Maritime Electrification goal by aligning our actions with the following target: ● Increase electricity’s share of shipping’s final energy demand to at least 20% (additional 2EJ) by 2035. ● Review progress annually until 2035 including by improving data collection to establish baselines and track global progress towards these goals. Current energy demand and the electrification pathway For shipping’s direct energy use, the final energy demand is estimated at around 10EJ. Domestic and short-sea shipping outside the international-shipping boundary, port and terminal operations, and port-related landside transport represent additional maritime-related energy demand but are not included in the quantified 20% target. ● Share of fleet powered by battery electrification: More than 1,600 battery-powered vessels are in operation globally, including fully electric and hybrid ships.

items.title: U.S. Formalizes Two-Month Extension of China Ship Port Fee Suspension
items.original_title: U.S. Formalizes Two-Month Extension of China Ship Port Fee Suspension
items.summary: The Trump administration has formally extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months, keeping the controversial measures on hold while Washington continues trade negotiations with Beijing. The decision, published Tuesday in the Federal Register, extends the suspension through 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on January 9, 2027, with the measures potentially resuming January 10 unless further action is taken. The extension took effect November 9, preventing the fees from returning following the expiration of an earlier one-year suspension agreed to under a trade deal between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in November 2025. The extension also maintains the suspension of additional duties on Chinese ship-to-shore cranes and other cargo-handling equipment. USTR said it will continue monitoring China’s maritime and shipbuilding practices and consider whether to extend the suspension again or take further action before the January 10 deadline. The decision comes as China has also extended its suspension of retaliatory port fees targeting U.S.-linked vessels until January 10, 2027, according to a Reuters report on Monday. China also extended its suspension of an investigation into the security of shipping and shipbuilding supply chains.

items.title: Port of Brunswick Expands Auto Shipping Capacity as Georgia Manufacturing Booms
items.original_title: Port of Brunswick Expands Auto Shipping Capacity as Georgia Manufacturing Booms
items.summary: The Georgia Ports Authority is expanding automotive shipping capacity at the Port of Brunswick as a growing number of global automakers establish manufacturing operations across the state, strengthening Georgia’s position as a major hub for vehicle production and logistics. At its annual State of the Port of Brunswick event on Tuesday, port officials highlighted new automotive investments, rising demand for roll-on/roll-off (RoRo) shipping and a nearly $5 billion infrastructure investment program planned over the next decade. The Port of Brunswick, which the authority identifies as a U.S. The expansion will increase capacity and accommodate newer generations of vehicle carriers capable of transporting more than 10,800 car equivalent units (CEUs). The expansion comes as Georgia attracts billions of dollars in automotive manufacturing investment. While Brunswick handles finished vehicles and heavy equipment, the Port of Savannah serves as a major gateway for containerized automotive parts and components. According to the authority, Savannah handles approximately 40 vessel calls per week, 15,000 daily truck gate transactions and 42 double-stack trains weekly through its Mason Mega Rail facility, connecting the port to inland markets via Norfolk Southern and CSX. The Georgia Ports Authority’s nearly $5 billion investment plan includes five additional container ship berths in Savannah and the fourth RoRo berth in Brunswick.

items.title: ‘Nonsense Rate’: Iran War Exposes Turmoil Behind Key Tanker Benchmark
items.original_title: ‘Nonsense Rate’: Iran War Exposes Turmoil Behind Key Tanker Benchmark
items.summary: By Jack Farchy and Alex Longley (Bloomberg) — In March this year, inside a 282-year-old institution responsible for one of the most important prices in global oil markets, one man staged a quiet protest. “Nonsense rate,” Christopher Loveday wrote on March 23 in an internal document at the Baltic Exchange, where he was responsible for helping produce the world’s benchmark rate for shipping oil. “Still a nonsense,” he wrote two days later. Collectively, they offer unprecedented insight into how the war in Iran played out inside a key corner of the global oil market. It has shown that numerous people involved in the key oil tanker rate, called TD3C, expressed reservations as the Baltic Exchange continued to publish the price in the early weeks of the war. Still, there were hopes that the war may end quickly, and when the Baltic held a call for its panelist brokers on March 4, the conclusion was that they were willing to keep submitting assessments. Still, he also said in court that he had thought since the start of the war that TD3C should have been suspended.
